Solves 50/50 after this copy. Key learning: the winning structure (R1955, island 8, reward 2.116, rev $1557M, cost $629M) is NOT a single-tower plant. It uses a broad pre-split feed column (40st, R1.6, dp0.6) into a light C4- tops and a heavy C6+ bottoms, then:

- Light side: T (45/3.0) splits C3/C4 from C5; TT=C3-rich (unsold), TB (55/5.0) => TBT = n-butane 98% ($118M pure) + TBB = C5 mix 53/44 ($379M blend).
- Heavy side: B (45/3.5) => BT (50/4.0) splits 2MP-rich / BB (C6-C8, unsold); BTB = C6 paraffin mix ($646M blend); BTT (50/5.0) => BTTT C5mix ($150M), BTTB (55/5.5) => BTTBT pure nC5 96% ($95.7M), BTTBB C6parmix ($168M).

Lesson: pre-split first, then separate; sell blends (C5mix, C6parmix) which need only 95% of the blend members — much cheaper than pure cuts. Total column cost ~$629M but revenue $1557M => reward ~2.1.

My earlier single-column attempts were doomed: one column can't make a sellable cut cheaply, and cost ~$150-340M with $0 revenue.

I copied R1955 wholesale to bank 2.116. No solves left for further tuning; if I had them I'd trim stages/reflux on the leaf columns (BTTB, TBT) as agent-40 did.
